transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-01-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes (auto)
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Maya, Jon, Priya, Liam (Oceanside)
Shared artifacts: Redwood console deck (https://rwd.red/deck/ocn-demo), security summary (link shared in chat), sample benchmark sheet (drive: https://drive.example.com/ocn-bench)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer interested in pilot with 3 production routes, concerned about PII, latency targets for clinical triage, and cost allocation to product teams.

[00:00:05] Samir: "Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samir, AE on the account, with Leah who will do the console walkthrough and nerd out on the perf bits. How are we all?"
[00:00:14] Maya: "Doing well, thanks. We have a few folks from SRE and FinOps on. We want to see how Redwood's console helps with cost visibility across our chatbot and clinical summarization routes."
[00:00:22] Jon: "Yep quick note: our main worry is that the summarization route sometimes spikes latency under load and FinOps wants to tie cost back to product owners."
[00:00:31] Leah: "Totally, we'll show route-level telemetry and the per-route cost attribution — and how you can set alerts if a route crosses token or latency thresholds. I'll pull up a live demo of the usage table and the route dashboards."

[00:01:02] Leah: "Okay I'm in the console, top left is the workspace selector — make sure you pick 'Oceanside - prod' — um, I'm using demo data but its structured like your data. First panel is overall usage: tokens in, tokens out, median latency, and cost burn rate."
[00:01:25] [Background: minor audio - someone typing]
[00:01:30] Leah: "You can see here the 'routes' tab — we surface routes by name, last 7 days traffic, 95th latency, and cost per 1k tokens. The important bit: routes inherit model and quantization profiles so we show model-level and route-level cost side-by-side."
[00:01:46] Priya: "Can you break down by product team? We do chargebacks monthly and need per-team buckets, not just route names."
[00:01:52] Leah: "Yes — you can map routes to tags, and then use the attribution view to roll up by tag or owner. Here's the 'Cost Allocation' roll-up — we have grouping by owner tag, plus filters for region and deployment type (hosted, dedicated, private)."

[00:02:20] Jon: "How is the cost computed? Is it strictly per-token or do you include GPU hour amortization for Dedicated?"
[00:02:28] Samir: "Good question — cost is a combination. For hosted we use per-token unit economics, for Dedicated we amortize committed capacity and apply an effective per-token rate based on utilization. There are knobs in Optimize to tune batching and quantization recommendations which will change the effective unit cost."
[00:02:44] Maya: "So if we go Dedicated, we can get a predictable monthly bill but need to keep utilization high enough to justify?"
[00:02:50] Samir: "Exactly — that's the tradeoff. We'll show an example later where a 70% utilization commit yields X cents per token vs hosted pricing."

[00:03:08] Leah: "Back to the console — clicking a specific route opens an expanded dashboard: per-minute QPS, token distribution histogram, 95/99 latency over time, and a cost waterfall that splits model compute, caching savings, and networking."
[00:03:27] [00:03:30] Leah: "Note the orange band here is where KV cache hits reduced cost — if you enable prefix caching you see a drop in per-token compute cost right away. We sometimes see transcriptions in the console where KV cache is rendered as 'K V cash' in older speech parsers — ignore that, it's just transcription wobble in the demo data."
[00:03:46] Priya: "Does the waterfall show quantization impact? Our ML folks asked if 4-bit quant would reduce cost and change latency."
[00:03:53] Leah: "Yes — we surface quantization profiles as scenarios. You can click 'Simulate 4-bit' and it will show estimated cost reduction and a rough latency delta based on our kernel selection models. Important caveat: for some safety-critical routes you might prefer higher precision even if costs are up."

[00:04:20] Jon: "What about PII/data residency? Our clinical summaries contain PHI; we need to ensure tokens aren't persisted in logs and that audit logs show requester IDs."
[00:04:28] Samir: "We have private deployments and hosted with VPC egress options. Audit logs include token-level redactions and requester metadata; full security pack is in the chat. For a pilot we recommend Private or Dedicated with KMS integration so you control keys."
[00:04:41] Liam: "Can you show an example of the audit trail for a single request?"
[00:04:46] Leah: "Sure — open request trace, here's an example trace: route name, model variant, token counts, execution time broken into KV fetch, attention kernel, and outbound. There's also a redaction flag and a link to the masked prompt stored only in your VPC if you're on private."

[00:05:15] [00:05:20] Leah: "I'll now show the alerts — you can set an alert on route 95th latency > 750ms or cost per hour > $X. For your clinical triage route we might recommend a 500ms 95th latency SLO and a fallback policy to a cheaper model if latency violates SLOs to avoid complete failure."
[00:05:38] Maya: "Fallback is interesting — we worry about hallucinations if a cheaper model is used for triage."
[00:05:43] Samir: "Right — the fallback should be for non-critical non-diagnosis steps, or used with guardrail prompts. The console supports canary rollouts and traffic shifting for A/B validation so you can validate quality at scale."

[00:06:10] Jon: "On batch size and concurrency — if we batch too aggressively do we risk latency spikes?"
[00:06:15] Leah: "There's a tradeoff. Optimize suggests batching targets per-model and per-latency SLO. For low-latency UI routes we keep batch sizes small and concurrency higher; for background summarization we recommend larger batch sizes to save cost."

[00:06:40] [00:06:45] Priya: "We need reporting that ties to our billing system. Can we export per-route cost slices?"
[00:06:50] Leah: "Yes — there is an export feature: daily CSV or S3 dump with per-route breakdowns, token counts, effective per-token rate, and the allocation tag. Many customers push this to their finance pipelines for chargeback."

[00:07:12] Samir: "I want to show a short demo scenario — Leah will flip to three routes we've prepared: chat-bot, triage-summarize, and batch-claims. Each has different model families and traffic profiles."
[00:07:22] Leah: "Loading mock data... okay, chat-bot has high QPS, low tokens per call; triage has moderate QPS but high tokens per call and needs low 95th latency; batch-claims is nightly large-batch processing. See how the cost per route differs — chat bot higher requests but lower tokens so cost still modest; triage is the expensive one because of token length and preferred high-precision model."

[00:07:55] [00:08:00] Leah: "I'm toggling the 'Simulate Dedicated' toggle — this recomputes expected per-token cost by adding committed capacity amortization. For triage route, if you commit a 2-GPU pool and get 60% utilization, your effective token cost drops by roughly 35% vs hosted. But if utilization falls below ~40% the math flips."
[00:08:22] Priya: "Can you show the chart that maps utilization to per-token price? We want to show FinOps the sweet spot."
[00:08:28] Leah: "Yep — here's utilization vs effective price. We'll attach the exact numbers after the call. This is also where Optimize's recommendations shine — it suggests model + quantization + batching combos to hit desired spend targets."

[00:08:52] Jon: "One more thing: inference caching — if we have many similar prompts, how much do we save?"
[00:08:58] Leah: "In our demo data you can see the cache hit rate panel — chat-bot has ~20% hit rate and that corresponds to roughly a 12% compute reduction. For triage, prefix similarity is lower so cache helps less. We'll also show you how to tune a prefix policy to improve hits."

[00:09:30] [00:09:35] Maya: "What about multi-region routing? We serve EU and US; compliance requires EU data not to cross region for some patients."
[00:09:41] Samir: "Smart routing supports region policies — you can pin routes to regions or route by requester geo. Fallback can go to a same-region model variant. Also audit logs show region of execution per request."

[00:10:04] Leah: "Now a quick look at the Alerts & Rollouts page — here's a canary config: send 5% traffic to new model variant and watch quality metrics (we integrate evals and can run lightweight prompt sets to compute pass/fail rates). If quality drops beyond threshold we auto-roll back."
[00:10:24] Priya: "Do you store our eval prompts? We think about the privacy of those prompt sets."
[00:10:28] Samir: "If you use Private deployment we store them only in your account VPC; hosted can store encrypted copies integrated with customer KMS on request."

[00:10:50] [00:10:55] Jon: "Let's talk about instrumentation — how do we get our telemetry into Redwood so routes map correctly? We have an API tag system today."
[00:11:01] Leah: "You can tag requests at client SDK or via request headers. We also accept logs via our ingestion pipeline so SREs can map existing tracing IDs to Redwood request IDs for correlation. We provide a small init script and sample agent for typical Kubernetes setups."

[00:11:28] Samir: "I know you asked about latency targets — what's an acceptable SLO for the triage route? Maya, do you have a target in mind?"
[00:11:34] Maya: "We want 95th latency under 500ms for a triage summary when under normal load. During spikes mild degradation is ok but we need good visibility and fallback rules."
[00:11:43] Leah: "We can set that SLO and wire an alert to your pager. We'll also show a simulated spike and a configured fallback to a smaller model while preserving an out-of-bounds tag so you can review those outputs later for quality."

[00:12:10] [00:12:15] Leah: "Switching to the FinOps view: here's last month's spend by route. You can click into a route and see a daily time series, and under 'Cost Drivers' we show tokens, model compute, and cache effect. There's also a 'what-if' slider to simulate moving X% traffic to a cheaper model or enabling 4-bit quant."
[00:12:38] Priya: "The what-if slider looks useful. Can we model switching to a hybrid strategy: hosted for dev traffic, dedicated for peak production?"
[00:12:45] Leah: "Yes, that's a common pattern. You can model multi-deployment routing and see blended cost impacts. Also route-level tags let you separate dev vs prod traffic in reports."

[00:13:05] [00:13:10] Jon: "What about billing exports frequency? We need daily exports for our internal pipelines."
[00:13:14] Leah: "Daily CSV to S3 or direct integration with some billing connectors. We'll include the schema in the attachments. The CSV includes route_id, owner_tag, date, tokens_in, tokens_out, effective_cost_cents."

[00:13:36] Samir: "Quick aside on compliance: Leah, can you summarize the Private option differences?"
[00:13:41] Leah: "Private gives you a control-plane isolated to your VPC, no cross-tenant metadata leakage, dedicated audit logs, and KMS-managed keys. On-prem option fully air-gapped if required. We'll also provide the SOC2 artifact and our encryption-in-transit/off at rest notes in the security pack."

[00:14:10] [00:14:15] Maya: "On the pilot: we want to start small with three routes for two weeks and validate both latency and cost. After that we may expand. Is a two-week window enough?"
[00:14:21] Samir: "Two weeks is a fine smoke test; for statistical confidence on cost and tail latencies we prefer 4 weeks but we can start with two and extend. Leah will run a baseline synthetic run to give you initial numbers."

[00:14:45] Leah: "I'll note the pilot scope: chat-bot (light), triage-summarize (critical), batch-claims (background). For each we'll collect: token counts, 95/99 latencies, cache-hit rates, and cost per 1k effective tokens. Also we'll run a short A/B for triage to measure quality if we test quantization."

[00:15:12] [00:15:20] Priya: "One piece: can you show us how to set owner tags automatically from our service mesh? We use Istio currently."
[00:15:26] Leah: "Yes we have an Envoy filter example and a small sidecar snippet that grabs team labels and app name and attaches them as route tags. We'll share the snippet in the follow-up materials."

[00:15:50] Jon: "We have an internal custom model variant that we've tuned. Can Redwood serve customer-supplied models?"
[00:15:56] Samir: "For Private/on-prem, yes you can run your own model binaries on our runtime. For hosted we support loading containerized model artifacts with vetting; we have a model onboarding checklist. We'll coordinate with your ML infra to validate compatibility."

[00:16:20] [00:16:25] Leah: "Now demo a little deeper: click into the 'Route Diagnostics' tab — this shows a waterfall per-request: queuing, model encode/decode, attention run, and token emission. You can hover to see kernel selection (e.g., friendly name 'fused-attn-fast'). The idea is to give you precise hotspots for optimization."
[00:16:45] Maya: "In past demos we've seen kernel names that are meaningless to our team; can there be a mapping to simple labels?"
[00:16:50] Leah: "We have a glossary you can enable which maps kernel names to plain language impact notes (e.g., 'attention-heavy: optimize by shortening context or use quant profile X'). We'll attach that."

[00:17:12] [00:17:20] Jon: "Can the console show anomalies automatically? Like sudden token spikes from a bug or loop?"
[00:17:25] Leah: "Yes — anomaly detection flags sudden deviations in token counts or 95th latency; you can tune sensitivity. We also integrate with Slack/pager to push alerts and include a link to a pre-filled diagnostic query."

[00:17:48] Priya: "Show me one more thing — the cost forecast for the next 30 days based on current trends."
[00:17:53] Leah: "Forecast panel: here's projected spend with confidence band. You can overlay planned changes — e.g., enabling caching or moving 20% traffic to Dedicated — and see the adjusted forecast."

[00:18:18] [00:18:25] Samir: "Alright quick pause — any major outstanding concerns from the customer side?"
[00:18:30] Maya: "Main concerns: PII controls, predictable cost for triage route, and pilot success metrics. Also, we want to ensure our FinOps team can get daily chargebacks."
[00:18:40] Priya: "And can we get an example invoice mapping so accounting knows how it'll appear?"
[00:18:44] Samir: "Yes we'll include a sample invoice and the CSV schema."

[00:19:02] Leah: "I'll now do a quick micro-benchmark demo — simple synthetic requests to triage route to show latency distribution under a 50% load. Starting test — generating requests..."
[00:19:16] [00:19:20] Leah: "Results populating: median 210ms, 95th 480ms on hosted variant with our tuned kernels. When I switch to a Dedicated simulated node the 95th drops to ~360ms for same load due to reduced multi-tenant interference."
[00:19:43] Jon: "That's promising. Is that with caching enabled?"
[00:19:46] Leah: "No cache for this micro-bench — it's pure infer. For real traffic you likely get some cache wins depending on prompt reuse."

[00:20:05] [00:20:10] Priya: "If we move to Dedicated, what's the lead time for provisioning?"
[00:20:14] Samir: "Typical lead time depends on region and capacity, but 7-21 days is usual for a small pool. We offer burst-backed capacity in hosted in the interim."

[00:20:32] Maya: "Legal will want to review data flow diagrams. We'll need the architecture doc."
[00:20:36] Samir: "We'll attach the architecture and the data flow diagram in the follow-up email."

[00:20:50] [00:20:55] Leah: "One last feature: the cost anomalies tab — it scans route-level spend and suggests optimizations, e.g., enable prefix caching on routes with high repeated prefixes or switch model family for routes with low accuracy sensitivity."
[00:21:09] Priya: "Would Optimize be able to recommend exact percent traffic to move to cheaper variant while keeping error delta under X%?"
[00:21:15] Leah: "We provide estimated quality regressions from our eval suite but final decision is up to you; we can run controlled validation with your labeled prompts to get real numbers."

[00:21:38] [00:21:45] Jon: "A couple of quick technical Qs: what's the KV cache eviction policy? And can we control TTL?"
[00:21:51] Leah: "Eviction is LRU by default; you can tune TTL per-route or use an explicit policy to keep certain prefixes. We'll share the doc with the config options."

[00:22:10] Maya: "Okay this has been helpful. Let's recap next steps."
[00:22:15] Samir: "Recap: Samir will send Dedicated pricing tiers and sample invoice; Leah will run baseline perf and return benchmark sheet; Maya will confirm pilot routes and success criteria; Priya will send historical token usage. We'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to lock pilot scope."

[00:22:45] [00:22:50] Priya: "One last ask — can you include a short checklist of security items Legal will want? That helps speed procurement."
[00:22:55] Samir: "Yes — we'll include a security checklist (SOC2, ISO notes, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency)."

[00:23:10] Leah: "I'll also drop the Envoy filter snippet and the billing CSV schema in chat."

[00:23:20] Maya: "Thanks all — this was great. Looking forward to the materials. We'll aim to kick off pilot on Feb 10 if logistics align."
[00:23:29] Samir: "Perfect, we'll target to have materials in your inbox by Feb 2 and sync on Feb 3 for pilot signoff. Any final quick Qs?"
[00:23:38] [brief silence]
[00:23:42] Jon: "Nope, that's it from SRE. Thanks."
[00:23:46] Priya: "Thanks, bye."
[00:23:48] Samir: "Thanks everyone, bye."

End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings present (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache), some technical terms simplified by speakers, and speaker overlap is minimal.
